title: Defining and Calling Functions
objective: Define a function with the function keyword and call it with the right arguments.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A function is a named block of code you can run again and again without rewriting it. You create one with the function keyword, a name, parentheses, and a body wrapped in curly braces: function greet() { ... }. The code inside the braces only runs when the function is called.

The names inside the parentheses in a function declaration are parameters — placeholders for values the function needs. When you call the function, the values you provide in its parentheses are arguments, and they get matched to the parameters in order.
Defining a function does not run it. Nothing inside the body executes until the function is called by name, with parentheses, somewhere else in the program.
explanation.rule: function name(parameters) { ... } creates a function; name(arguments) is what actually runs it.

examples.title: Define, Then Call
examples.note: Nothing logs until the last line calls strikeAnvil with an argument.

checks.question: function greet(name) { ... } — what is name called inside the function declaration?

feedback.correct: Correct — name is a parameter, a placeholder filled in by whatever argument is passed when the function is called.
feedback.incorrect: The placeholder written inside a function's own parentheses is called a parameter; the actual value passed at call time is the argument.

assignment.title: Strike the Anvil
assignment.brief: Write strikeAnvil(times) that logs the exact text 'Striking ' followed by times followed by ' times.'
requirements: Use console.log to output the message.
Match the exact text, including the trailing period.

hints: function strikeAnvil(times) { ... } defines the function; times is the parameter.
Use + to join the pieces: "Striking " + times + " times."
strikeAnvil(3) should log exactly: Striking 3 times.
